messages:
Ana Rodriguez: Quick RFC follow-up: we need to finalize autoscaler semantics for Dedicated GPU pools (orch + policy) before the next infra sprint.
Matt Chen: Summary of goals: keep p99 inference latency within SLOs, avoid runaway cost, and minimize tail spikes from cold model loads. Signals we should consider: gpu_util_pct, pending_queue_len, model_loads_per_min, pending_kv_cache_bytes, node_preemption_rate.
Sophia Patel: +1. Important to separate control plane decisions (scale decisions) from placement heuristics (packing, eviction). We can allow the autoscaler to request N GPUs, and the placement engine decides packing.
Ryan O'Neill: For placement, we should support two packing modes: strict-isolation (one model per GPU) and densify (binpack multiple small models). Densify needs a robust kv_cache reservation and CUDA-context accounting to avoid OOMs.
Matt Chen: Proposed hysteresis: require metric breach for two consecutive windows before scaling up; and require stabilization_window (default 180s) before scaling down. Also limit step size: max_scale_up = ceil(current_replicas * 0.5) and max_scale_down = floor(current_replicas * 0.3).
Sophia Patel: We also need a notion of prewarm/standby slots for cold-start-heavy models. Config options: prewarm_count (int), prewarm_policy (none|model-aware|tiered). Model-aware prewarm pins a warm process for specific high-QPS models.
Ana Rodriguez: Cost control: allow a customer-level budget cap and a safety throttle that prevents autoscaler from exceeding monthly spend delta X% without manual approval. Also expose predicted cost delta before aggressive scale-ups.
Ryan O'Neill: On node types: allow mixing on-demand and spot (preemptible) GPUs. For spot pools we should add more aggressive headroom to avoid SLO violation on preemption. Example: keep 2 on-demand proxies per pool for critical traffic and use spot for burst capacity.
Matt Chen: Fallbacks: when scale fails or queue saturates, route to fallback model variants: quantized variant, shorter context pass, or CPU fallback if configured. Fallback decision rules: if scale_attempt_failed AND queue_len > fallback_threshold -> route to fallback_x.
Sophia Patel: Also track fallback_ratio and have an alert trigger: if fallback_ratio > 0.03 for 10m -> paging oncall and mark pool for scaling review.
Ana Rodriguez: Example policy YAML (staging experiment):
```
policy_name: dedicated-stg-v2
signals:
  - gpu_util_pct
  - pending_queue_len
  - pending_kv_cache_bytes
  - model_load_count_per_min
targets:
  gpu_util_pct: 0.70
  pending_queue_len: 40
bounds:
  min_replicas: 1
  max_replicas: 40
cooldown_seconds: 45
stabilization_window_seconds: 180
max_scale_up_fraction: 0.5
max_scale_down_fraction: 0.3
prewarm:
  type: model-aware
  prewarm_count: 1
placement_hints:
  packing_mode: densify
  gpu_vendor: nvidia
  min_memory_gb: 32
  kv_cache_safety_factor: 0.85
  disallow_mig: false
```
Matt Chen: Implementation notes: 1) autoscaler should emit a planned_replicas field before actually making API calls so we can run a placement dry-run and estimate cost. 2) avoid thrashing by committing scaling operations only after placement dry-run success.
Ryan O'Neill: We need eviction semantics when packing: prefer unloading least-recently-used small models on the same GPU, prefer unloading non-critical models that have cold replicas elsewhere. Also ensure we respect pinned models (customer pinned min_replicas).
Sophia Patel: Tests we should add to infra repo:
- spike test: 10x RPS for 3 minutes; verify p50/p95/p99 and that planner proposes sufficient scale-ups.
- KV-pressure test: repeatedly load large kv caches until memory approaches safety factor, verify densify refuses new placements.
- preemptible node loss: simulate losing 30% of pool nodes while under load.
- cold-start mix: 50% new-model loads interleaved with steady traffic.
Ana Rodriguez: Rollout plan: dry-run in staging pool (pool-id=ded-stg-4) for 72h, collect cost delta and tail latency, then canary 2% prod for 1h, then 10% for 6h, gated by monitoring.
Matt Chen: Observability: add metrics - proposed_replicas, scale_decision_latency, placement_dryrun_success, fallback_ratio, prewarm_utilization, per-model_kv_bytes, packing_rejections. Dashboards and SLO gates for canary.
Ryan O'Neill: Automation: when fallback_ratio > threshold and placement dry-run indicates capacity can be added within budget, autoscaler should optionally request an emergency scale-up but gate by an approval flow if cost impact > budget_threshold.
Sophia Patel: Edge cases: model eviction races, model version incompatibilities (can't co-locate model v2 and v3 if they use conflicting CUDA flags), and node heterogeneity leading to performance variance. We should annotate nodes with perf_profile and let placement prefer stable matches.
Ana Rodriguez: Security/compliance note: for Private deployments, prewarm must respect tenant isolation — prewarm slots can't be shared across tenants. For shared Dedicated, allow shared prewarm with workload labeling.
autoscaler-bot: dry-run applied policy dedicated-stg-v2 to pool ded-stg-4. dry-run_id=ci-1730001200. logs: https://ci.redwood/infra/autoscale/1730001200
Matt Chen: Action items:
- @Sophia: push policy YAML to infra repo and create staging dry-run job (ETA: today EOD).
- @Ryan: add per-model kv bytes metric and a placement API that returns packing feasibility (ETA: Tue).
- @Ana: write a short RFC addendum listing fallback tiers, alert thresholds, and budget gate semantics (ETA: Fri).
Ana Rodriguez: Will capture these in RFC doc and follow up with perf model numbers. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
